## 1. What was read

**865 research articles** from 33 of the 33 journals on the roster.

A further **291** records (25% of the 1,156 this month's harvest returned) carry no abstract and are not research: news, correspondence, editor highlights and obituaries. PubMed types them `Journal Article` and nothing else, so the publication-type filter cannot see them — across the whole index they are 22.7% of it and 35% of `general`, and 3,801 of them are JAMA. Every count below is over the full harvest and is inflated by this; the figure above is not.

!!! warning "Volume swing against the median month: sysbio +29%"
    Check the source before reading anything into this. Two benign causes account for most of these. `bioinfo` every January carries the Nucleic Acids Research database issue and runs high. And several journals simply deposit nothing in some months: across the 44 months read, 4 of 33 journals are absent from at least one, worst being *Nat Mach Intell* (20 months missing, 81 papers in total) and *Bioinformatics* (4 months missing, 2,905 papers in total). Every journal on the roster contributed this month. Queried directly, PubMed returns zero for those journal-months too — the holes are in the source, reproduced exactly by re-running the harvest. So a swing here is not evidence that a field went quiet, and is not usually evidence that the pipeline broke either.

Largest contributors: Nature 123, JAMA 115, Nucleic Acids Res 94, Science 84, Bioinformatics 74, Lancet 64.

## 3. The evidence that moved it

**The heaviest month for foundation-model refutations the corpus had recorded to
this point, and the form has changed.** Ten cards, and three of the five read
here replace the model with a trivial baseline and watch the number stay put:
classical molecular fingerprints with shallow classifiers
[match or beat protein language models](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/41981726/) on
peptide function; ML and deep survival models
[fail to beat Cox baselines](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/41992491/) on low-dimensional clinical data; and
structure-aware substitution models built on predicted structures
[do not improve on plain sequence models](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/42036821/).
[scArchon](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/42121287/) is the fourth and is more mixed than it was carded:
across nine perturbation-response predictors on six single-cell datasets,
performance is heterogeneous — trVAE, scGen, scPRAM and scVIDR are robust across
multiple datasets, while others *occasionally* fall below linear or control
baselines, and models with favourable aggregate scores can still lose the
biological perturbation signature, which is the finding that matters. The fifth,
[42020757](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/42020757/) (*Nature*), is about the scoring rather than the model:
accuracy-scored LLM benchmarks reward confident fabrication rather than
measuring truthfulness.

!!! note "Corrected 2026-08-27"
    This section carried a paragraph headed "ctDNA took two more hits, one of
    them a landmark". One of the two was not a hit.
    [TOMBOLA](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/41544704/) was carded from a title
    that gives the trial, the intervention and the population and no endpoint,
    and a failure was supplied for it. The trial met its primary endpoint. The
    Galleri item is a news report rather than a trial paper, and it was credited
    with mortality evidence the trial never collected. Both are restated below.

**TOMBOLA is the strongest single result the ctDNA-as-guide claim has.**
[41544704](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/41544704/) (*Ann Oncol*) monitored 178 assessable patients after
neoadjuvant chemotherapy and radical cystectomy for muscle-invasive bladder
cancer with tumour-informed ctDNA, and started atezolizumab on ctDNA positivity
irrespective of imaging. It met its primary endpoint: 60% (50 of 84) of treated
ctDNA-positive patients reached molecular and radiographic complete response.
Median lead time from ctDNA detection to imaging-confirmed recurrence was 90
days, and one-year recurrence-free survival was 97% in ctDNA-negative against
76% in ctDNA-positive patients. It is single-arm phase II, so it cannot say what
would have happened without the atezolizumab — but ctDNA is the treatment
trigger here, not a prognostic label, and that is the thread's claim.

**The Galleri item is trade reporting, and its point is about endpoints.**
[41817436](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/41817436/) is a *Cancer Discovery* news report, not a trial
readout: NHS-Galleri, the randomised trial of the multi-cancer early detection
test, missed its primary endpoint of a reduction in late-stage cancers, and
researchers quoted in the piece attribute that partly to the trial's use of a
surrogate endpoint rather than cancer-specific mortality. Mortality was never
measured, so no mortality evidence was withheld or delivered; the criticism is
of the design, and it is the same surrogate-endpoint problem this corpus tracks
on the treatment side.

**And the month's real negative for the thread is the one that worked.**
[41616224](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/41616224/) (*JCO*) applied a tissue-free ctDNA assay to 2,260
patients from Alliance N0147 and found strong independent prognostication —
disease-free survival hazard ratio 5.03, five-year DFS 27.7% against 77.1%, with
tumour fraction stratifying further inside the positive group. The assay
performs. It counts against this thread because the thread's claim is that ctDNA
is more than prognostic, and here a large, well-executed application stops at
risk stratification. Taken together the month reads: ctDNA detects reliably and
early, a prospective trial has now acted on the detection and met its endpoint,
and the month's largest cohort by an order of magnitude still uses it only to
sort patients.

**Anti-TIGIT got a defence rather than a result.** [41564381](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/41564381/)
(*JCO*) argues that the original anti-TIGIT antibodies failed on Fc isotype
design — unmutated IgG1 — and that the target was therefore never properly
tested. The record in this index is a commentary title with no abstract, so the
argument is all there is to read, and it is an argument that withholds judgement
on the target rather than delivering one: the card is neutral. Note its
structure. The same manoeuvre — the target survives by relocating the blame to
the format — has now been applied to CD47, TIGIT and CTLA-4 in this corpus, and
it is the kind of claim that decides whether `next-gen-checkpoints` gets
reopened rather than the kind that settles it.

**Interception found a second causal variable, alongside the mutation.**
[41781610](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/41781610/) (*Nature*) shows that the stress response of nascent
squamous tumours in the mouse upper gastrointestinal tract instructs the
underlying mesenchyme to build a precancerous niche: stimulated fibroblasts
mount a wound-healing response that remodels the extracellular matrix into a
fibronectin-rich scaffold, and heterotypic 3D culture and grafting show that
the niche *alone* is sufficient to confer tumour properties on carcinogen-free
healthy epithelium. The paper's own model is that mutations and the stromal
response to them **together** define whether an early lesion persists — not the
niche instead of the clone. Read with February's finding that premalignant
colorectal lesions are polyclonal in origin, the direction of 2026 is that the
unit of interception is larger than a single mutant cell.

## 4. Refutations

### (a) Landing on a tracked thread

[41701973](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/41701973/) (*Blood*): across 584 patients given CD19 CAR-T for
large B-cell lymphoma at six Australian centres, time of infusion is not
associated with outcome once confounders are accounted for. It is a clean null
on a chrono-immunology hypothesis that a 2025 card had supported for allogeneic
transplant, and it is recorded because the corpus should not accumulate only the
positive half of a fashionable idea. It is not, though, a card against cell
therapy: infusion timing is incidental to this thread's claim about
generalisation beyond CD19-positive B-cell disease, and counting a null on an
incidental variable as a refutation of the platform is how a thread acquires a
negative it never earned. The card is now neutral.

### (b) Method credibility

Fifteen cards, thirteen of them refutations and two now neutral. Of the four
read here, only two are measurements. [41882360](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/41882360/)
(*Nature*) uses negatively supercoiled DNA minicircles and cryo-EM to show why
supercoiling drives Cas9 off-target cleavage: the HNH domain is held in a more
catalytically competent conformation, new DNA-RNA mismatch geometries are
accommodated across the protospacer, and plasticity in the PAM-distal region is
topology dependent. What the card previously added — that standard specificity
assays cannot see this — is a methodological verdict the paper does not state,
and it has been removed. It is the third editing-safety card in seven months,
after November's [heritable impairment after repair](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/41196998/) and
December's [epigenetic disruption by double-strand breaks](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/41331675/).
[42141119](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/42141119/) (*Nat Biotechnol*): DNA off-targeting confounds
RNA-chromatin occupancy assays, making a body of published RNA-chromatin maps
artifactual.

!!! note "Corrected 2026-09-04"
    This opened "Four cards, and only two of them are measurements." Four was the
    whole month on this thread when May was carded from titles; the 2026-09-04
    abstract re-scan puts it at fifteen — thirteen refutations, which is the
    `−13` in section 2, plus the two cards earlier corrections moved to neutral.
    The four discussed here are described correctly and the half-are-measurements
    observation holds of them. What is withdrawn is the implication that it holds
    of the month: eleven cards on this thread are not read in this briefing at
    all, and nothing here licenses a claim about their composition.

The other two of the four are not. [42133765](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/42133765/) (*Science*) is a policy piece
arguing that genetic quality control for mouse lines should be modernised; its
abstract is a single sentence and it reports no measurement. The claim carded
from it — that unmonitored drift is a hidden artifact behind irreproducible
phenotypes — is plausible and was supplied by the reader, not by the paper, and
it is now neutral.

!!! note "Corrected 2026-08-27"
    This subsection also read
    [42129548](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/42129548/) as an independent
    finding that analysis results shift with software package choice and
    version, and called it "the second month in a row with that finding, after
    April's [41903535](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/41903535/), now from a
    different journal and a different data modality". It is a *Nature Methods*
    research highlight, single author and no abstract, and what it summarises is
    41903535 itself. There is one study here, not two in successive months, and
    no second journal or modality. The card is now neutral.

What survives that correction is still worth naming. The audit genre spent 2025
moving from the model to the pipeline to the instrument, and April's 41903535
moved it to **the version number** — the claim is no longer that a method is
wrong, but that the same method on the same data gives a different answer
depending on when you ran it. That is one paper, given a second airing as a
research highlight in another journal, and it should be carried at the weight of
one paper until something independent lands on it.
